speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what is the average teacher-student ratio for primary, secondary and junior college levels respectively; (b) what efforts are being taken to reduce class sizes and increase the ratio of teachers to students; and (c) how will the Ministry further alleviate teachers of administrative duties to allow them to focus their day in school on teaching.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I note that he has raised this issue before, in fact, as early as October 2013 – I dug it out.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is comparable to many Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries and better than countries, such as the United States (US), United Kingdom (UK), Germany, Korea and Japan.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, PTR and class sizes are different concepts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: PTR measures resourcing, that is, the total number of teachers provided against the student enrolment numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On the other hand, the class size reflects how we deploy our teachers, that is, how much teaching they conduct vis-à-vis out-of-classroom activities, such as curriculum planning, conducting co-curricular activities (CCAs), or attending professional development training.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It also reflects whether teaching resources are deployed evenly for all students or varied depending on the needs of the students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Once we differentiate the two concepts, we will realise that there are only two ways to reduce class sizes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One is to stick to existing resourcing levels but give teachers more teaching load and reduce their out-of-classroom activities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I visited a French primary school recently that is run that way.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It has a PTR of 19:1 – much less resources compared to Singapore, but it has class sizes of 15 to 20 – smaller than Singapore's.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is able to achieve this because it deploys its teachers fully for teaching.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Given that resourcing is a zero-sum game, it means the French school may not have a lot of resources for lesson preparation, CCAs, learning journeys, teachers' training, as well as dedicated help for students with specific learning needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A second way is to expand the teaching force so that we can have the best of both worlds – small class sizes, without undermining out-of-classroom activities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But that has significant budgetary implications, especially given that manpower is the largest cost component of our education budget.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Remember, our resourcing level is already at OECD standards.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Furthermore, a big increase in recruitment will also alter the quality of the teaching force – inevitable, when you try to recruit in such big numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is also difficult to sustain, in our context, given increased manpower demands in other sectors, such as healthcare and the needs of the economy, all competing for the smaller and smaller cohorts of adults entering the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But where we can, we deploy teaching resources to help students with a greater need for teachers' guidance.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, the Ministry of Education (MOE) allocates additional teachers to our schools based on their student profiles and to allow them the autonomy to organise class sizes appropriately.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the secondary schools, for example, while Express classes are mostly taught in class sizes of close to 40, Normal (Technical) classes for some subjects are commonly sized at 20.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In NorthLight School, Assumption Pathway School, Crest Secondary School and Spectra Secondary School, students are taught in class sizes of 20.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Over the years, MOE has taken steps to also ease teachers' administrative duties through the use of technology to streamline processes through e-platforms, such as Parents Gateway and the use of apps for attendance-taking.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE will continue to introduce additional measures and better leverage technology to reduce the administrative workload and other demands on our teachers' time, such as on lesson preparation and marking, to allow them to focus their day in school on teaching.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I agree that ensuring, maintaining high quality in our educators must be an over-riding factor.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If classroom sizes can be reduced while quality of teaching remains high, that is an ideal win-win.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The tradeoffs will take time to iron out.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the meantime, my question is: can MOE please invest in Allied Educators and administrative support staff to ease the load on the teachers such that teachers can focus on teaching to the benefit of students?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Career progression for the Allied Educators and administrative support staff is also key.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My second supplementary question: in the way the Ministry of Health (MOH) is building up capability in the allied health worker force to aid the doctors in performing their duties, would MOE also build up training and continuing professional development for allied educators or even set up an Allied Educator Academy, so that teachers can be very ably partnered by Allied Educators in the education of our young?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In fact, in my visits to schools, usually the top suggestion from teachers is, “Can we have more help from Allied Educators?”, partly to help them teach as teaching aids, but also to help them deal with, sometimes, disruption in class.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the same time, as we recruit more, we will also have to look at their career paths, career progression as well as their professional training.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Minister, since there is a decline in the birth cohort and classes, the number of students is actually getting fewer and fewer.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Do they go into preschools other than the NorthLight Crest and Spectra?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How can they be deployed elsewhere to support an even better quality of education?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My second question: there is a lot of talk about administrative duties of teachers, of educators.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Can the Minister define what are administrative duties?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, if educators work with parents, partner parents or they take on duties to encourage students to come to school or work with delinquents and spending time, are those considered administrative duties?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Is teaching currently defined as just being in front of the classroom or just doing the academics?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I reported improving pupil-teacher ratio (PTR) and one big driving force of that improvement is really because of falling cohort sizes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, we always provide for enough resourcing but let the schools have the flexibility to deploy the resources to help the students that need it most.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for the administrative duties, I thank the Member for that question.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think every teacher has a great role to play beyond the classroom – working with parents, sometimes guiding the students outside of the classroom, and going out of their way to make sure they help students.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think we can use technology to better handle them.
